what_this_is: The owner scope of every table a migration of this repository creates (A1-10). TableOwnershipTest reads it: a migration that creates a table absent from this file fails, and an entry no migration creates fails too, so the register can neither fall behind the schema nor keep a name the schema has dropped.

scopes.global: One row set serves the whole platform. There is nothing per country to carry.
scopes.country: The row belongs to one of the six markets and says so in a column of its own.
scopes.storefront: The row belongs to one storefront. The storefront key is the ISO country code today (A1-09 records that it has no identity of its own yet).
scopes.legal_entity: The row belongs to one selling company.
scopes.customer: The row belongs to one customer identity, which GCC-13 keeps single across markets.
scopes.seller: The row belongs to one seller or shop.
scopes.warehouse: The row belongs to one inventory location.
scopes.provider_account: The row belongs to one carrier or fulfillment provider account.
scopes.channel_account: The row belongs to one marketplace account.
scopes.derived: The row carries no owner column: it reads one through the parent `by` names. Discovery 03 counts about 150 tables of this kind, and giving each a country_id instead is what DECISIONS guardrail 3 forbids.
scopes.inherited: Created by the single-market platform, before an owner scope was a question anyone asked of a table. Its scope is NOT decided, and deciding it is A1-10's remaining work. No NEW table may be classified this way: the guard pins this set, so it can only shrink.

rules: Every table any migration creates has an entry here.
Every scope other than `global` and `inherited` names in `by` the column, or the path through a parent, that carries the owner.
`inherited` is frozen: the guard fails when a table is added to it.
A migration that passes a variable to Schema::create cannot be read statically, so it names its tables in `declares`.

address_city_aliases.why: normalized_alias is unique across every country today, which H1-10 records as a collision waiting for a second country

audit_logs.why: The panel audit trail, one table for every market. G1-08: each line names the market it concerns since 2026_12_29_100000; a line written before that names none, which is the honest record rather than a guessed Saudi Arabia.

channel_attention_reviews.by: source with source_row_id: the row under review carries the owner

checkout_idempotency_keys.why: 'customer:<id>' or 'guest:<id>': the key is claimed by whoever pressed submit, so two people may hold the same idempotency key and one person cannot submit it twice (D1-326).

customer_registration_claims.why: 'email:<address>' or 'phone:<number>', one row per identity across every market as GCC-13 requires. The row is written BEFORE the account exists -- user_id is filled by whichever concurrent payment confirmation wins -- so the owner is the identity rather than a user id (D1-328).

failed_jobs.why: One queue serves the whole platform, and the row carries no owner column: connection, queue, payload, exception, failed_at. The PAYLOAD of a failed job may well concern one market, but the sink deliberately is not narrowed by it -- whoever is on call must see every failure, and a per-market failure sink would hide one market's failures from the person reading another's. `jobs` beside it is `inherited`, which this register freezes, so a new companion cannot join that set.

inventory_locations.by: id; the shelf itself now names its market and its selling company (storefront_country, legal_entity_id; 2026_12_27_100000)
inventory_locations.why: G1-05 recorded that the anchor carried no country, which was true when it was written: the only way to ask which market a stock figure belonged to was through the PRODUCT, which answers for the units and never for the shelf. InventoryLocationMarket reads the column now, by StorefrontMarketRows' rule, and an unmarked row is the default storefront's.

legal_entities.by: id, one row per country (country unique)

myfatoorah_webhook_events.why: an inbound event is stored before its owner is known; the attempt it dedupes to carries the storefront

notification_channel_profiles.by: country, '' being the shared row every market falls back to
notification_channel_profiles.why: The account a storefront's messages leave through, one per channel per market (I1-01, I1-02), unique on (channel, country). The '' row is the account every market falls back to and NOT a seventh market, which is the convention integration_settings already uses for the carriers (H1-11); it defaults to '' rather than NULL because two NULLs differ in a unique key, and is ascii_bin on MySQL and MariaDB so a market is compared byte for byte. SETTLED after four readings disagreed, and both of the first arguments were wrong. Mine was that it is `country` because it names no legal entity beside it, unlike payment_gateway_accounts -- false: storefront_legal_documents is `storefront` by country_code and names none either. The other was that `storefront` is what every market column is filed as -- also false: address_regions, admin_country_scopes and the two routing-rule tables are all `country`. What decides it is A1-09: the storefront key is the ISO country code only FOR NOW. So the question is which owner this row would follow once a storefront has an identity of its own -- the shop, or the country as a jurisdiction. A sending account belongs to the shop, as a payment gateway account does; a routing rule, a region and an employee's countries belong to the jurisdiction. Hence `storefront`.

odoo_account_mappings.why: H2-10: the entity that should own the mapping has no column; odoo_company_id is a number in a config, not a legal_entities reference

odoo_posting_queue.by: source_type with source_id: the cost entry or statement row being posted

platform_admin_audit_logs.why: as above; G1-08 asks for the country each line concerns, which is not built

platform_admin_devices.why: as the grants and sessions above: a device belongs to a platform admin's session, not to a market. The topics it is subscribed to name markets, and the grant decides which, but the row itself is platform-wide

platform_admin_grants.why: the platform administrator is not a market actor: a grant is platform-wide by design

product_destination_permissions.by: product_id -> products.storefront_country, with destination_country naming the far side

provider_fulfillment_items.by: storefront_country, with fulfillment_account_id naming the carrier account (2027_01_02_100000)
provider_fulfillment_items.why: C-04: the line was derived through provider_fulfillment_id, which answers which carrier and never which market. A row written before that migration names neither, and OwnershipHistory is the written rule for reading one: the default storefront, and the carrier's platform-wide account. Nothing backfills, because that emptiness is what tells a pre-market order from a Saudi one.

sales_channel_accounts.by: id; its market is derived from its settings (ChannelAccountCountry), not stored

shipping_rule_drafts.by: target_country, with source_country naming where the draft was copied from

subscriptions.by: storefront_country, NULL being the default storefront's
subscriptions.why: The newsletter list, one table for every market (I1-04). A signup records the market the visitor was on since 2026_12_31_100000; a row written before that names none, and NULL is read as the DEFAULT storefront's -- an unmarked subscriber signed up on the only storefront there has ever been. That is the OPPOSITE of the notifications.storefront_countries convention, where an unmarked row means every market, and the difference is the difference between a setting and a message: an unmarked broadcast was SENT to everybody and still is. Scope storefront rather than country on the A1-09 reading settled for notification_channel_profiles: a marketing list belongs to the SHOP a visitor subscribed to, as a sending account does, and not to the country as a jurisdiction. It leaves inherited because it now names a real owner, which is the only direction that bucket moves.
